newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed firm on tight supply, USDA news.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed firm on tight supply, USDA news.

text.p: Rapeseed in northern Europe steadied after a decline over the new year period because of tight supply and in sympathy with bullish U.S. data, brokers said.
Hamburg spot sellers were at 470 marks and trade buyers around two marks lower for Jan/Feb while mill buyers had not emerged, they said.
Jan prices three weeks ago, before the Christmas holidays, had been in a 464/467 marks buyer/seller range.
New crop free Hamburg was at 437.50 marks and trade buyers five marks lower.
Chicago soybeans were looking for gains after the release of bullish USDA ending stocks figures.
Severe winter conditions in Europe may threaten winter rapeseed in the ground after Germany lost one third of its rapeseed crop in the harsh 1995/96 winter, traders said.
Although damage in Germany to date should be limited, neighbouring Poland, a swing buyer or seller, is hit far worse and may need to import from Germany again.
Better prospects for soft oils demand in Rotterdam and a firm dollar were also cited as supportive factors.

But on the downside, rapeseed crush margins are still unattractive, given the rape oil premium over soy oil -- today at 1.75 guilders per 100 kilos fob mill-- and the ready availability of soybeans, and this despressed trade volumes.
Jan rapeseed buyers at points other than Hamburg were broadly steady in a 450-468 marks range while the new crop market, in a 415-439 marks range, was roughly ten marks higher than three weeks ago.
The Matif futures exchange attracted good volume with May up nine marks at 468 and Feb up ten at 465.
First quarter rape oil sellers were at a steady 84.50 marks per kg.
Local rape meal sellers (34 percent protein) raised prices per 100 kg by 1.25 to 32.00 marks for Jan, while Fab/April meal was at 30.25 marks, up 0.50. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
